lines.text: Weigh it? Rub it on stone? Still guessing.

hooks: How do you pay with a coin when nobody knows what's in it?
Nobody trusted money. This is one of the earliest known coins of pure gold.
One of the earliest known coins of pure gold exists because nobody trusted money.
One of the earliest known pure-gold coins exists because the gold coins before it were a gamble.
This coin is about 1.6 centimetres long, and one of the earliest known coins of pure gold.
loop_note: Line 14 'Trust: solved. Before that...' runs into line 1 on restart: 'Before that... how do you pay with a coin when nobody knows what's in it?' Final frame (gold coin dropping into the trader's palm) matches frame 1 (pale coin landing in the same palm, already in motion at t=0 with the first caption on screen at t=0).
changes: Line 1 kept word for word (panel pick, 83/100); first caption at t=0 over a coin already landing in the palm.

0-9 s: line 2 'This is one of the earliest known coins of pure gold.' The real Met stater appears as line 2 starts (~4.9 s) and the superlative is said once, in full, by ~9 s. It says what the coin is, not how it got that way, so the 'how' stays open until the refinery beats.
HIGH mark 7.3-11.5 fixed: label dump removed. 'About 8 grams' dropped; 'found at Sardis' dropped from the coin and Sardis moved to the refiners (line 6), where it says where the fix happened.
Problem beats: 'Before it, coins mixed gold and silver.' / 'How much? Nobody knew.' replace the frowning trader with a split-coin picture and two traders comparing shades.
Refinery montage kept (salt / baked / silver drew off / basically pure); this is where the hook's 'how' gets answered.
Silver confusion fixed: 'Stamp a lion and bull.' (gold strike) then 'Pure silver got its own coin. Same stamp.' (separate silver strike, side-by-side labelled GOLD / SILVER).
Hedges kept: 'one of the earliest known', 'Croesus gets the credit'; no 'first ever', no claim that Croesus made this coin, no weight given.
